Just present, constant, wearing. The road narrows past the last farmsteads and becomes something older. Rutted. Poorly maintained. Nobody comes this way for pleasure.Frizwick rides with her collar up and her eyes moving. Habit. She can't turn it off any more than you can.Morwen has the fieldwork journal out across her saddle. Reading while she rides. Somehow not dropping it.Daeris rides quietly. She does that well.Three hours out, the last visible rooftop of Sandpoint drops below the southern horizon. Just road and scrub and the mountains ahead, still distant, still patient.The road forks twice before midday. Both times the northern branch is the right one. You take them without hesitation.By early afternoon the ground starts rising. Subtle at first. Then less subtle. The horses feel it. The dark bay mare tosses her head once and settles."First night camp," Frizwick says, "before dark. While we can still see what we're sleeping next to."Sound advice. Rock walls on both sides, uneven, plenty of ledge. Classic. If you were setting an ambush, you'd use this ground.You move up the left side, low, using the rock. Nothing on the ledge above. Scuff marks in the dirt, but old ones. A week at least.You cross to the right side.There. A hollow in the rock face, shoulder-height. Fresh marks around the lip. Someone sat here recently. Waiting. Boot prints in the frost, two sets, pointing toward the road.They left. Or they're further ahead.Two people. One heavier than the other. They moved north along the ridge, not down to the road. Parallel to your route. Watching it rather than blocking it.Scouts. Or something that thinks like scouts.You get back to the horses. Frizwick reads your face immediately."How many?" she says."Two. Ahead of us. Watching the road from the ridge."Morwen closes the journal.Daeris says nothing. Just looks north, toward the cut, toward whatever's waiting on the other side.🔊………

Two shapes.Not moving to intercept. Just watching.Then the cut spits you out the other side and the road opens up again, wider, scrub on both flanks, sky overhead. You don't stop. The mare's flanks are steaming."They didn't move," she says."No.""So they're reporting, not blocking.""That's what it looks like."Morwen brings her horse around.
